title: Orsen and the Letters
premise: Juniper Dravenmoor, a cellist whose career shattered on stage three years ago, inherits half of a failing orchard in the valley town she fled a decade ago — co-owned with Orsen Vale, the boy she abandoned and never stopped rehearsing an apology to. Forced into a harvest season of shared labor, legal standoffs, and small confessions, they discover the deed was manipulated by the orchard's foreman, who has been quietly stealing the land's profits for years. When Juniper chooses to expose him publicly — risking her fragile anonymity and Orsen's family legacy — she finally speaks the sentence she has rehearsed for ten years, and the two choose each other as the first grapes come in.
about_author: Casper Delacroix is the pen name of a former orchard hand turned novelist who writes love stories set against stubborn land and stubborner people. Their work explores how justice, like fruit, ripens slowly and only when tended.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Three years after her catastrophic final performance, Juniper receives notice that she co-owns Vale Orchard with Orsen Vale — the name she left behind a decade ago. She drives back intending only to sign away her share, but the deed refuses transfer: a clerical knot no lawyer can untangle quickly. Emotional beat: dread curdling into reluctant curiosity as she sees the orchard, and Orsen, still standing.

chapters.title: Rows We Never Finished
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Trapped by the deed through harvest season, Juniper and Orsen work the rows together, trading barbed memories and discovering the ledgers don't add up — someone has been skimming the orchard blind for years. Juniper plays cello again for the first time, alone, at dusk. Emotional beat: old tenderness rekindling under suspicion, both realizing the other may be the only honest thing left here.

chapters.title: What the Foreman Buried
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. They uncover proof the foreman forged the original deed to keep the Vales and Dravenmoors from comparing records — and he's now threatening to burn the season's crop if they go public. Orsen wants quiet justice; Juniper, testing her rebuilt courage, insists on exposure before the harvest festival. Emotional beat: love and duty colliding as Orsen realizes protecting Juniper means letting her be brave.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the festival, before the whole valley, Juniper presents the evidence, ending the foreman's hold on the orchard — then takes the stage where she once failed and says the sentence she rehearsed for ten years: that she left out of fear, not lack of love. The crowd, and Orsen, listen. Emotional beat: catharsis and belonging; the first grapes come in as they begin again, together, on land that finally belongs to both.
